meanings.Name: the record set's name, for people
meanings.MedRDSVersion: the version of the standard that new files are checked in under
meanings.TimeZone: the IANA time zone whose local time the file names carry
meanings.RecordIdSystem: the URI of the system the record IDs come from
meanings.Kinds: kinds of one's own beside the standard's vocabulary, each with a Description and Labels by language
meanings.KeepOnceAbove: the size in bytes above which a file is kept once: the store of versions then holds a pointer to it, not a second copy
meanings.Language: the language the place writes in, as a BCP 47 tag: that of every file that does not say otherwise
meanings.Facility: the place of treatment as other systems know it: its Name, its Identifier, the Type of facility and the practice Setting, each of these a code with its System
meanings.ExchangeCodes: the codes a copy for another system carries: international (LOINC) or de (IHE Germany); international where nothing is said

meanings.Source: the SHA-256 of the version it was drawn from
meanings.Method: how it was drawn: one word of the list of methods
meanings.MadeWith: the program that drew it, with its version
meanings.Made: when it was drawn, in UTC
meanings.Language: the language the text was read in, as a BCP 47 tag, where the method needed to be told
meanings.Pages: the text, one string for each page where the source has pages, else one
meanings.Values: the values read, each with where it was read

text.description: the text a file holds as text: the text of a PDF, of a word processor's document, the body of an e-mail
text.example: the text of a letter that came as a PDF

ocr.description: text recognised in pictures of writing: a scan, a photo of a page
ocr.example: the text of a scanned discharge letter

speech.description: text recognised in a recording of speech, as the program heard it; a transcript that a person checked is a part of its entry
speech.example: the words of a voice message, for searching

values.description: values read out of a file to be taken over elsewhere, the results of a laboratory report for instance: proposals, until a person takes them over
values.example: the potassium of a photographed laboratory report, with the line it was read from

valueParts.page: REQUIRED where the source has pages

valueMeanings.printed: the line the value was read from, as it was read
valueMeanings.page: the page it stands on, counted from 1
valueMeanings.box: where it stands on that page: left, top, right and bottom, in points from the top left corner of the page as it is shown

meanings.Reference: the document and the version it was read from, as a result names them (medrds:<record ID>/<document ID>/<version>)

kindGroups.documents: Documents: what is written about the patient, here or elsewhere
kindGroups.assessments: Assessments: what the patient or the physician filled in or worked out by a fixed instrument
kindGroups.recordings: Recordings: where the picture, the sound or the signal is itself what is documented
kindGroups.meddav: From medDAV: the patient's card and appointments as medDAV holds them, the source of the results it keeps

note.description: the physician's own note on a consultation or a call
includes: the note on a first consultation
a note on a telephone call
the note drawn from a recorded session

excludes.what: a finding written as a report
a letter to a colleague

codes.why: IHE Germany: the KDL maps the code of a progress report to the class BRI (letter); its map was made for the archives of hospitals.

report.description: a finding or report, one's own or received

excludes.what: laboratory results
the pictures or the recording the report is about
a report sent as a letter between physicians
a single value as data

codes.why: The class 26436-6 is a set of studies, as all classes of FHIR R4 for studies are.

letter.description: a letter between physicians, received or sent
includes: the letter of a family doctor
one's own letter to a colleague

excludes.what: a letter to or from the patient, an insurer or an authority
the referral itself

codes.why: The class 34133-9 is the summary of an episode, which a letter between physicians mostly is; for a discharge letter the type 18842-5 says more.

referral.description: a referral, an admission to hospital or a request for a consultation

excludes.what: the answer that comes back

includes: a certificate of incapacity for work
an attestation for a school or an employer
a certificate for compensation of disadvantages

excludes.what: a report for an authority that states findings

else.for: a certificate of incapacity for work
a certificate of incapacity for work

codes.why: LOINC has no active code for every certificate: 80571-3 (Certificate) is discouraged; each kind of certificate has its own. No class of FHIR R4 fits.

prescription.description: a prescription of medicines, remedies or aids

excludes.what: the medication the patient takes, as data

else.display: Prescription for Medical Equipment or Product

else.for: a prescription of remedies or aids

codes.why: No class of FHIR R4 fits a prescription.

plan.description: a plan of treatment with a schedule of its own
includes: a medication plan as printed and handed out

excludes.what: the medicines the patient takes, as data
what was agreed in a consultation

codes.why: The class 56447-6 of FHIR R4 is deprecated in LOINC, and no other fits.

questionnaire.description: a questionnaire filled in that is not a rating scale

excludes.what: a rating scale with a result

codes.why: LOINC has one type for questionnaires and rating scales alike, 74465-6, and no class of FHIR R4 fits either: read back, these codes name neither kind.

scale.description: a rating scale or psychometric test, filled in, with its result

excludes.what: a score worked out by the physician from findings
the report that interprets several tests

else.for: a scale of depression such as BDI-II

codes.why: LOINC has one type for rating scales and questionnaires alike, 74465-6, and no class of FHIR R4 fits either: read back, these codes name neither kind.

score.description: a clinical score worked out from findings

excludes.what: a scale the patient fills in

codes.why: LOINC has no type for a clinical score; 51848-0, an evaluation note, comes closest. No class of FHIR R4 fits.

image.description: a picture: a photo, a scan of a picture, a study from radiology
includes: a photo of a skin finding
an MRI study as a folder

excludes.what: a document that was scanned or photographed
the report on a study

codes.why: LOINC tells a photo (72170-4) from a study of radiology (18748-4) and has no code for both; the class 18726-0 of FHIR R4 is for radiology alone.

audio.description: a sound recording and its transcript
includes: its transcript as transcribed and as corrected

excludes.what: the note drawn from a recorded session

codes.why: LOINC has no type of document for a recording of sound, and FHIR R4 no class (FHIR R5 has the media category audio).
LOINC has no type of document for a video, and FHIR R4 no class. The KDL has a code for videos of operations alone and gives a video the code of a picture.

signal.description: a recorded signal of the body

excludes.what: the report on the recording

codes.why: LOINC has a type for each kind of recording (EEG, ECG, polysomnography) and none for all; the class 27897-8 of FHIR R4 is for neuromuscular studies alone.

card.description: the patient's card as medDAV holds it, master data and clinical values, a vCard 4.0
includes: the card with the lasting diagnoses, the allergies and the medication
the card as it was each time its clinical values changed

excludes.what: a medication plan as printed and handed out
a letter that names diagnoses

codes.why: No classification has a type of document for a person's card: it is master data, with the results drawn from documents.

event.description: an appointment or journal entry as medDAV holds it, with its clinical values, an iCalendar object
includes: an encounter with its diagnoses, findings and notes
a journal entry with the values of a laboratory report that came by post

excludes.what: the laboratory report itself
the physician's note written as a document

codes.why: No classification has a type of document for an appointment as data: it is the encounter as medDAV holds it, with what came of it.

consent.description: a consent, its withdrawal or restriction; a release from confidentiality

codes.why: The class 57016-8 of FHIR R4 is for consent to a privacy policy alone, and fits no other consent; a release from confidentiality has codes of its own.

correspondence.description: letters, e-mails and applications to and from the patient, insurers, authorities

excludes.what: a letter between physicians
an invoice

else.for: letters to and from an insurer

codes.why: The class 47049-2 of FHIR R4 is deprecated in LOINC, and no other fits.

invoice.description: an invoice for treatment, a reminder, a receipt

codes.why: No class of FHIR R4 fits an invoice.

disclosure.description: a copy of the record, or of a span of it, that went out
includes: the copy given to the patient

codes.why: No class of FHIR R4 fits a copy of a record.

loinc.name: LOINC
loinc.checked: every code and its long common name looked up on HL7's terminology server (tx.fhir.org), against LOINC 2.83: active, and of the scale Doc for types

kdl.name: KDL
kdl.checked: the FHIR package dvmd.kdl.r4 2026.0.0 of the DVMD: its code system, and its two maps to IHE Germany (kdl-ihe-classcode, kdl-ihe-typecode)

ihedClass.name: IHE-D classCode
ihedClass.checked: the FHIR package de.ihe-d.terminology 3.0.1 of IHE Germany, and ART-DECOR

ihedType.name: IHE-D typeCode
ihedType.checked: the FHIR package de.ihe-d.terminology 3.0.1 of IHE Germany, and ART-DECOR

ihedFacility.name: IHE-D healthcareFacilityTypeCode
ihedFacility.checked: the FHIR package de.ihe-d.terminology 3.0.1 of IHE Germany

ihedSetting.name: IHE-D practiceSettingCode
ihedSetting.checked: the FHIR package de.ihe-d.terminology 3.0.1 of IHE Germany

format.name: IHE FormatCode
format.checked: the code system IHE FormatCode of IHE

snomed.name: SNOMED CT
snomed.checked: the example value sets of FHIR R4 for the kind of facility and the practice setting (c80-facilitycodes, c80-practice-codes)

exchange.classes: the Document Class value set of FHIR R4 (http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/document-classcodes, 4.0.1), 46 codes of LOINC; FHIR R5 has dropped it

international.description: classCode and typeCode from LOINC, where the kind has them

de.description: classCode and typeCode of IHE Germany, as the KDL maps the kind's code to them

attributes.from: the version's xmpMM:InstanceID as an OID under 2.25
the record ID, assigned by the RecordIdSystem of medrds.json: its URI as an OID under 2.25, by way of a name-based UUID of it
Patient.json: the name and the date of birth
the extension of the file, by the schema's table of media types
urn:ihe:iti:xds:2017:mimeTypeSufficient: the media type says what the format is
the SHA-1 of the file, worked out when it goes: in hexadecimal in XDS, in base64 in FHIR
the size of the file in bytes
the name of the document in the package
the file's dc:language, else the Language of medrds.json
the Type of the Facility in medrds.json
the Setting of the Facility in medrds.json
the moment the package is made
who makes the package, and the Name of the Facility
the Identifier of the Facility where it is an OID, else the name of the record set as an OID under 2.25
a new UUID as an OID under 2.25
for whom the package is, else the patient's name

DTM.meaning: a moment in UTC, as precise as it is known; a date alone as YYYYMMDD, YYYYMM or YYYY, as far as it is known

CX.meaning: an identifier with the OID of whoever assigned it

XCN.meaning: a person: the whole name in the place of the family name, since medRDS does not take a name apart

XTN.meaning: an address of e-mail; one author, one person, one address

coded value.meaning: a Classification: the code as its nodeRepresentation, the OID of its system in the slot codingScheme, its display as its Name

OID under 2.25.meaning: a UUID as one decimal number after 2.25 (ITU-T X.667); a URI first as a name-based UUID (RFC 9562, version 5, in the namespace of URLs)

layout.README.TXT: who made the package, when, with what, and what it holds; its lines end in CR LF, as a medium has them
layout.INDEX.HTM: the documents with their dates, kinds and titles, linked, for whoever has a browser (XHTML Basic 1.1)
layout.IHE_XDM/SUBSET01/METADATA.XML: the metadata of every document, as XDS writes them: one SubmitObjectsRequest of ebRIM 3.0
layout.IHE_XDM/SUBSET01/DOC00001.PDF: the documents, under names of ISO 9660 level 1 that any medium takes: DOC, five digits, and three letters of the extension in upper case

fields.meaning: the title of the name, or longer
the kind of the name
the type of the document in a classification, where it says more than the kind: the system and the code, divided by a vertical bar
who wrote it: the physician, the laboratory, the sender; one or more people or bodies
the body the authors wrote for: a hospital, a practice, a laboratory
who took responsibility for the content, by signing it or releasing it
free text; tags
the language of the content, as a BCP 47 tag; where it is not said, that of the record set
where the document itself can be found again: a DOI, a URL, the message ID of an e-mail, the sender's reference
the program; for transcripts and drafts the model
the date and time of the name, with the offset from UTC; the date alone where the time is not known
when this version's metadata were written
the same for all versions of a file
one per version
the previous version: its document ID, its version ID, the file name it was filed under and its SHA-256
one event per version: what was done, when, by whom, what changed; where the version settles a fork, the SHA-256 of the versions it sets aside (settles)
the record ID at the time of filing
when and by whom it was checked in
where the file came from: the channel, the sender, when it arrived, the name and hash it had
fields.example: { channel: "email", from: ["Dr. Hans Hausarzt <mailto:praxis@hausarzt.example>"], received, name, sha256 }

fields.meaning: in a restriction: the document IDs it restricts
how confidential the content is, a code of HL7: N normal, R restricted, V very restricted; normal where it is not said
of an entry that is a folder: every file of the folder, with its path in it, its size in bytes and its SHA-256

a copy of each card of an address book that a person or body of the metadata is named with (7.2), as it was when the file was filed: a vCard 4.0 as its text, with its UID; who they are and how they are reached, nothing else
the version of the standard it was checked in under

meanings.channel: how the file came: one word of the list of channels
meanings.from: who or what it came from; REQUIRED where the file came from outside
meanings.received: when it arrived, where that differs from the clinical date
meanings.name: the name the file had before check-in; REQUIRED where it had one
meanings.sha256: the SHA-256 of what the file was before check-in; REQUIRED where it existed before
meanings.bound: where several files were bound into one at check-in: each of them, in the order of the pages, with its name and its SHA-256; REQUIRED there

written.description: written here by a person, in a program
written.example: a note typed after a consultation

program.description: made here by a program: a certificate issued, a transcript, an export
program.example: a certificate that the practice software issued

device.description: recorded here by a device: a camera, a recorder, a measuring instrument
device.example: a photo of a skin finding

post.example: a hospital's letter, scanned on arrival

fax.example: a laboratory report sent by fax

email.description: came by e-mail, of whatever kind
email.example: a colleague's letter as an attachment

download.description: fetched from a portal or a website

handover.description: brought along or handed over, on paper or on a medium
handover.example: a CD with an MRI study that the patient brought

schemes.mailto: an e-mail address: the identifier to prefer, unique and a way to reach the person
schemes.https: a web address: a practice's page, a profile, an identifier of a register such as ORCID
schemes.urn: an identifier of a register that has no web address
schemes.acct: an account of the program in use; only where nothing else is known

cards.meaning: the card of an address book that holds the person or body, by its UID: urn:uuid: and a UUID, compared without regard to case, or urn:x-contact-uid: and any other UID, compared as written

DESCRIPTION_MISSING.remedy: Write medrds.json; without it a program cannot tell that the folder is a record set.

DESCRIPTION_INVALID.finding: medrds.json cannot be read, or lacks a REQUIRED field
DESCRIPTION_INVALID.remedy: Put the file right and file it; the version before stays in the store.

ROOT_UNKNOWN.finding: something at the top that the standard does not name
ROOT_UNKNOWN.remedy: Move it out of the record set, or into _inbox if it is to be checked in.

RECORD_FOLDER_NAME.finding: a folder at the top that is not named as a record
RECORD_FOLDER_NAME.remedy: Name it family name, given names, date of birth and record ID; or move it out.

RECORD_ID_CHECK.finding: a record ID whose check character is wrong
RECORD_ID_CHECK.remedy: The ID was mistyped. Take it from the patient's card or from Patient.json.

RECORD_ID_TWICE.finding: two records with the same ID
RECORD_ID_TWICE.remedy: If they are one person, merge them; if not, one of them carries a wrong ID.

PATIENT_MISSING.remedy: Write Patient.json for the person the folder is named for.

PATIENT_INVALID.finding: Patient.json cannot be read, or is no FHIR Patient
PATIENT_INVALID.remedy: Put it right and file it; the version before stays in the store.

PATIENT_MISMATCH.finding: folder name and Patient.json name different IDs
PATIENT_MISMATCH.remedy: Find out which is right before anything else is filed here.

NOT_CHECKED_IN.finding: a file or folder in a record whose name is not that of an entry
NOT_CHECKED_IN.remedy: Check it in: it gets its name, its metadata and its place in the store of versions then.

DATE_INVALID.finding: a date or time that does not exist
DATE_INVALID.remedy: The entry was named by hand. Check it in anew under the right date.

VERSION_NAME.finding: something in the store of versions that is not named as a copy or as a pointer
VERSION_NAME.remedy: It was put there by hand. Move it out; the store is written by programs alone.

DERIVED_NAME.finding: something in _derived/ that is not named as a derived file
DERIVED_NAME.remedy: It was put there by hand. Move it out; what lies in _derived/ is written by programs alone.

COMPANION_ALONE.finding: a sidecar, a signed form or a container without its file
COMPANION_ALONE.remedy: The file it belongs to was renamed or removed. Bring the two together again.

WITHDRAWN_REMAINS.finding: a tombstone of an entry beside files of that entry
WITHDRAWN_REMAINS.remedy: Taking the entry out was not finished: move the remaining files to the trash.

CASE_COLLISION.finding: two names that differ only in case or normalisation
CASE_COLLISION.remedy: Give one of the two another title; on many file systems only one of them can exist.

META_MISSING.finding: a REQUIRED field of the metadata is absent
META_MISSING.remedy: The file was not checked in, or by a program that does not write the field. Check it in, or file it as a new version.

META_INVALID.finding: a field of the metadata is not in the form the standard asks
META_INVALID.remedy: Write the field in its form, in a new version.

META_NAME_MISMATCH.finding: date, time or kind in the metadata differ from the name
META_NAME_MISMATCH.remedy: The file was renamed after it was filed. Find out which of the two is right.

META_WRONG_PATIENT.finding: the file names a patient who is not this record's: filed with the wrong patient
META_WRONG_PATIENT.remedy: Take the entry out of this record and check it in with the patient it names.

META_CHAIN_BROKEN.finding: a version names one before it that the store does not hold, or one that is another document
META_CHAIN_BROKEN.remedy: The copy of the earlier version was removed from the store, or the later one was not made from it. Compare with backups.

CARD_MISSING.finding: a person or body is named with a card of which the metadata hold no copy
CARD_MISSING.remedy: File a new version of the metadata with a copy of the card as the address book holds it, or name the person without the card.

CARD_CONTENT.finding: a copy of a card holds what does not belong in it: a photo, a key, properties of secDAV, or properties of medDAV other than the identifiers of practitioners and bodies
CARD_CONTENT.remedy: File a new version of the metadata with the copy made anew: who the person is and how they are reached, nothing else.

CARD_UNUSED.finding: a copy of a card that nobody of the metadata is named with
CARD_UNUSED.remedy: Name the person with the card, or leave the copy out of the next version of the metadata.

FILE_MISSING.finding: a newest version whose file is not in the folder
FILE_MISSING.remedy: The file was removed or renamed by hand. Put it back from the store, or take the entry out if that was meant.

VERSION_DAMAGED.finding: a copy whose content is not what its name says, or a pointer that cannot be read
VERSION_DAMAGED.remedy: The copy was changed after it was filed. Bring it back from a backup.

FOLDER_CHANGED.finding: an entry that is a folder whose files are not as its sidecar lists them
FOLDER_CHANGED.remedy: A file in the folder was changed, removed or added. Bring the folder back from a backup, or from where it came.

BOUND_MISSING.finding: a PDF that pictures were bound into that does not hold, in the version that was bound, each of them as its origin names it
BOUND_MISSING.remedy: The PDF was changed after it was bound, or its origin names pictures it never held. Take the version that was bound from the store, or bind the pictures again from where they came.

KIND_UNKNOWN.finding: a kind neither in the vocabulary nor declared
KIND_UNKNOWN.remedy: Declare the kind in medrds.json, or use one of the vocabulary.

NOT_FILED.finding: a file named as an entry that has no version in the store: laid in by hand, waiting to be checked in
NOT_FILED.remedy: Check it in: it gets its metadata and its first version then.

FORMAT_CHANGED.finding: a file named as an entry that has no version, lying where a file of the same entry under another extension lay, which is gone: waiting for a person to say whether it is that one's next version
FORMAT_CHANGED.remedy: Say whether it is: a program then files it as the next version of the other (8.1.4), or puts the other back, or checks this one in by itself.

DERIVED_ORPHAN.finding: a derived file of content that no version in the store has
DERIVED_ORPHAN.remedy: It was drawn from a file that was never filed, or its entry left without it. Delete it; a program draws it again where it is wanted.

FILE_CHANGED.finding: a file that is not as its newest version: changed outside, waiting to be filed
FILE_CHANGED.remedy: File it as the next version. The version before is in the store.

VERSIONS_FORK.finding: two versions of a file that stand beside each other, and no later version that settles which holds
VERSIONS_FORK.remedy: They were filed at the same time in two places. Decide which holds, or bring them together, and file that: the new version names the one it follows, and sets the other aside.

DERIVED_DAMAGED.finding: a derived file whose content is not what its name says, or that cannot be read
DERIVED_DAMAGED.remedy: Delete it; a program draws it again where it is wanted. Nothing of the record is lost by that.

NAME_LONG.remedy: Shorten the title of future entries; containers that encrypt names may have to shorten this one.

PERSON_TWICE.finding: two records with the same name and date of birth
PERSON_TWICE.remedy: Merge them if they are one person, or note in both that they are two.

CONSENT_MISSING.finding: a recording in a record without a consent filed no later than it
CONSENT_MISSING.remedy: File the consent; if there is none, the recording should not be there.

LITTER.finding: a file that an operating system or an open program left behind
LITTER.remedy: Delete it, once the program that left it is closed.
